base_population.note: All shares in this file are conditional on the 18+ civilian population, NOT the total resident population. The schema's child brackets ('Under 5', '5-12', '13-17') are deliberately absent from age_bracket. See the 'adult_only' warning below - a pool containing minors MUST be filtered before raking or every adult margin is silently skewed.

notes: Shares are population shares within US adults 18+, so each calibrated dimension sums to 1.0 over the schema categories it supplies. calibration.rake_weights normalizes each margin over the codes actually supplied and treats negative codes as missing, so a dimension that omits a category which really exists in the population does NOT degrade gracefully - it reallocates that category's mass across the categories that remain. Every dimension here therefore enumerates all schema values, using a small explicit share rather than omission for rare categories. Dimensions that cannot be responsibly enumerated are left with empty shares and are skipped by the raking script.

adult_only.reason: rake_weights counts every row with a non-negative code in the margin denominator. A minor carries a valid age code, so leaving minors in the pool inflates the denominator and pushes all adult shares down uniformly while the minors keep unadjusted weight.

geography.note: The MatrAIx schema has no country dimension. The finest geographic value is region='North America', which pools the United States, Canada and Mexico. There is no way to isolate US residents from persona dimensions alone.
geography.operationalization: The raking script selects region='North America' and, optionally (--us-culture), narrows to cult_united_states in [Native, Lived there]. Both are proxies. 'North America' over-covers (Canada ~40M, Mexico ~130M adults); the cult_united_states narrowing under-covers, because that dimension is sparsely populated and defaults to 'Unfamiliar'.
geography.consequence: Results from this target set describe 'North American adults reweighted to US marginals', not a US probability sample. Do not report them as US population estimates.

provenance.method: Hand-authored from recalled published figures. NOT machine-derived from primary microdata.
provenance.network_note: The authoring environment had no route to census.gov, api.census.gov, bls.gov or fred.stlouisfed.org (all blocked by the sandbox egress proxy), so no figure here was fetched or reconciled against a source file.
provenance.verification_status: UNVERIFIED. Shares are approximations good to roughly +/-1-2 percentage points on the well-measured dimensions and materially worse on the ones marked quality 'low'. They are fit for pilot work, method development and plumbing tests. Regenerate from primary sources before any published estimate.
provenance.regeneration: Rebuild from ACS 1-year PUMS (age, sex, educational attainment, race/Hispanic origin) and CPS ASEC (employment, marital status), following the pattern of persona/curation/existing_data/scripts/derive_targets_ph.py. The urbanicity and socioeconomic_band splits are not census constructs and need an explicit crosswalk decision, not a table lookup.

sources.age_sex: US Census Bureau, Vintage 2023 national population estimates by age and sex; adult base derived as total resident population minus under-18.
sources.education: US Census Bureau, Educational Attainment in the United States (CPS ASEC table series), population 25 and over.
sources.race_ethnicity: US Census Bureau, ACS 2023 1-year estimates, race and Hispanic origin, adult population.
sources.urbanicity: US Census Bureau 2020 Census urban/rural classification (80% urban / 20% rural) for the urban-rural split; the within-urban decomposition is a MatrAIx schema-prior judgment, not a census figure.
sources.employment: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey, 2023 annual averages (labor force participation, full/part-time status, self-employment).
sources.marital_status: US Census Bureau, America's Families and Living Arrangements (CPS), 2023, population 18 and over.
sources.political_lean: Gallup annual ideology averages (conservative / moderate / liberal), 2023. Not an official statistic and not a census margin.

age_bracket.reference: Census Vintage 2023 age estimates, renormalized to the 18+ base
age_bracket.coverage: complete over adults - child brackets deliberately absent, see adult_only

gender_identity.reference: Census binary sex for adults (women slightly over half, rising with age); non-binary tail from Gallup/Pew LGBT identification estimates
gender_identity.coverage: The census sex item cannot enumerate Non-binary / Self-described / Prefer not to say. Unlike the Philippines target set, these are given small explicit shares rather than omitted, because omission would reallocate their mass to Woman/Man. The three tail values are estimates, not measurements.

highest_education.reference: CPS educational attainment, population 25+, crosswalked to the 10-value schema ladder
highest_education.coverage: Two known distortions. (1) Base mismatch: published attainment is for 25+, but this target is applied to 18+, so it understates the share of 18-24s still short of a degree. (2) 'Vocational / cert' is not a CPS category; its share is carved out of 'some college, no degree' by judgment. 'Postdoc' is a position rather than an attainment level and is given a near-zero placeholder so it is enumerated rather than omitted.

demo_ethnicity_broad.reference: ACS 2023 race and Hispanic origin for adults, crosswalked to the schema's 10 broad groups
demo_ethnicity_broad.coverage: The schema's categories do not align with OMB race/ethnicity. Two judgment calls dominate: the single ACS 'Asian' group (~6.2% of adults) is split into East / South / Southeast Asian using national-origin composition, and 'Middle Eastern' is carved out of the census 'White' category, which is where MENA respondents are currently tabulated. Hispanic/Latino is treated as mutually exclusive with the race groups.

urbanicity.reference: 2020 Census urban (80%) / rural (20%) anchor; within-urban decomposition is a schema-prior judgment
urbanicity.coverage: Only the 80/20 urban-rural split is an official figure. The Census Bureau does not define 'suburban', and the Dense urban / Suburban / Small town decomposition below is a judgment call that self-identification surveys (which run closer to 27/55/19 urban/suburban/rural) would not reproduce. Treat this margin as shaping, not measurement; it is included in the defaults because urbanicity strongly conditions cost-of-living items, but it is the weakest of the five.

demo_employment_status.reference: BLS CPS 2023 annual averages, forced into the schema's single-valued status
demo_employment_status.coverage: ADVISORY - not in default_rake_dimensions. CPS statuses overlap in ways the schema does not: a self-employed person is also employed, students often work part-time, and 'Gig / freelance' has no CPS definition. Forcing one primary status per persona makes these shares a modelling choice rather than a measured marginal.

demo_marital_status.reference: CPS 2023 marital status for adults 18+, with the never-married group subdivided by judgment
demo_marital_status.coverage: ADVISORY - not in default_rake_dimensions. CPS measures Married / Widowed / Divorced / Separated / Never married. The schema's 'Single', 'In a relationship', 'Engaged' and 'Domestic partnership' are a subdivision of never-married that CPS does not publish; that subdivision is estimated.

political_lean.reference: Gallup 2023 ideology averages, expanded from a 3-point to the schema's 6-point scale
political_lean.coverage: ADVISORY - not in default_rake_dimensions. Ideology is self-reported and not an official statistic. Gallup measures conservative/moderate/liberal; splitting those into Left / Center-left / Center / Center-right / Right and adding 'Apolitical' is an interpolation. Calibrating economic-attitude research on a political margin also risks assuming part of what the study is trying to observe - opt in deliberately.

socioeconomic_band.reference: no official marginal exists for this construct
socioeconomic_band.coverage: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and the safe state. 'Low income' through 'High income' is a subjective band with no published US distribution to calibrate against - Pew's lower/middle/upper tiers (roughly 30/51/19 of households) are household-level, tier-defined by local median income, and do not map onto five persona-level bands. Supplying a guess here would be actively harmful for an economic-pressure study, because household finances are the dependent variable: raking on them would bake the finding into the sample. The raking script skips a dimension whose shares are empty.
